title: Altered Mental Status Differential Diagnosis
description: Differential diagnosis for altered mental status (AMS) in adults presenting to the emergency department, covering neurologic, toxicologic, traumatic, infectious, metabolic, and psychiatric etiologies. AMS accounts for approximately 5% of ED visits with a 9% mortality rate.
source_description: Kanich W, Brady WJ, Huff JS, Perron AD, Holstege C, Lindbeck G, Carter CT. Altered mental status: evaluation and etiology in the ED. Am J Emerg Med. 2002;20(7):613-617.

diagnoses.name: Stroke / Intracranial Hemorrhage
key_features: Focal neurological deficits (hemiparesis, aphasia, facial droop)
red_flags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (Cushing triad)
recommended_tests: CT angiography if ischemic stroke suspected

diagnoses.name: Meningitis / Encephalitis
recommended_tests: Head CT (before LP if focal deficits or papilledema)
Empiric antibiotics (do not delay for imaging)

diagnoses.name: Sepsis / Systemic Infection
key_features: Known or suspected source of infection (UTI, pneumonia)
Elderly patients may present with AMS as sole sign of infection

diagnoses.name: Hypoglycemia
key_features: Confusion progressing to obtundation or seizures
History of diabetes or insulin/sulfonylurea use

diagnoses.name: Drug / Alcohol Intoxication
key_features: History or evidence of substance use
Alcohol odor on breath or elevated ethanol level

diagnoses.name: Alcohol / Benzodiazepine Withdrawal
key_features: History of chronic alcohol or sedative use with recent cessation

diagnoses.name: Traumatic Brain Injury
key_features: History of head trauma or mechanism of injury
External signs of head trauma (lacerations, hematoma)

diagnoses.name: Seizure / Post-Ictal State
key_features: Witnessed seizure activity or tongue biting
History of epilepsy or subtherapeutic antiepileptic levels
red_flags: New-onset seizure in adults (consider structural lesion)

diagnoses.name: Metabolic / Electrolyte Derangement
red_flags: Severe hyponatremia (< 120 mEq/L) with seizures or coma

diagnoses.name: Psychiatric Disorder
key_features: Intact vital signs and normal physical exam
red_flags: First psychiatric presentation in elderly (always exclude organic cause)

diagnoses.name: Hyperglycemic Crisis (DKA / HHS)
red_flags: Cerebral edema (especially in young adults with DKA)

diagnoses.name: Delirium (Acute Confusional State)
key_features: Inattention (unable to sustain or shift attention)
red_flags: Hypoactive delirium often missed (quiet, withdrawn patient)
Delirium as sole presentation of serious illness in elderly

also_consider.name: Non-Convulsive Status Epilepticus
also_consider.rationale: Prolonged unexplained AMS with subtle or no motor findings; requires EEG for diagnosis and is commonly missed

also_consider.name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
also_consider.rationale: Headache and confusion in multiple household members or during winter months; co-oximetry required as pulse oximetry is falsely normal

also_consider.name: Wernicke Encephalopathy
also_consider.rationale: Classic triad of confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia in malnourished or alcoholic patients; administer thiamine before glucose

also_consider.name: Thyroid Storm / Myxedema Coma
also_consider.rationale: Hyperthyroid or hypothyroid crisis with AMS; check thyroid function tests in unexplained encephalopathy

also_consider.name: Adrenal Crisis
also_consider.rationale: Refractory hypotension and AMS in patients on chronic steroids who abruptly discontinued; treat empirically with hydrocortisone

also_consider.name: Hypertensive Encephalopathy / PRES
also_consider.rationale: Severely elevated blood pressure with headache, visual changes, and confusion; MRI shows posterior white matter edema

also_consider.name: Serotonin Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Triad of AMS, autonomic instability, and neuromuscular hyperactivity after serotonergic medication change; clonus is key finding

also_consider.name: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Hyperthermia, rigidity, and AMS after dopamine antagonist use; elevated CK and requires dantrolene

also_consider.name: Toxic Alcohol Ingestion (Methanol/Ethylene Glycol)
also_consider.rationale: Elevated osmolar gap with AMS; methanol causes visual symptoms, ethylene glycol causes renal failure; require fomepizole

also_consider.name: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
also_consider.rationale: Young women with psychiatric symptoms, seizures, and movement disorder; associated with ovarian teratoma; check CSF antibodies

also_consider.name: Hepatic Encephalopathy
also_consider.rationale: Confusion with asterixis in known liver disease; elevated ammonia level; may be precipitated by GI bleeding or infection

also_consider.name: Hypothermia
also_consider.rationale: Core temperature < 35C causing progressive confusion to coma; J-waves on ECG; common in elderly and homeless patients

also_consider.name: Hypoxia / Hypercapnia
also_consider.rationale: Respiratory failure causing AMS; check pulse oximetry and blood gas; COPD exacerbation is common precipitant

clinical_reasoning_prompt: This is an evidence-based reference set, not an exhaustive differential. Use the AEIOU-TIPS mnemonic (Alcohol, Epilepsy/Electrolytes/Encephalopathy, Insulin, Opiates/Oxygen, Uremia, Trauma/Temperature, Infection, Poisons/Psychogenic, Stroke/Seizures) to systematically broaden the differential. Always obtain point-of-care glucose immediately. Consider occult trauma (subdural hematoma) in elderly and anticoagulated patients, polypharmacy effects, and that delirium is often multifactorial. A diagnosis of psychiatric cause requires exclusion of all organic etiologies first.
